newsitem.title: USA: Radisys says allegations have no substance.
newsitem.headline: Radisys says allegations have no substance.

text.p: RadiSys Corp said there is no substance to allegations of financial discrepancies related to a wrongful termination lawsuit and it has voluntarily provided information to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission regarding these allegations.
RadiSys said the litigation is currently in the discovery phase, with certain documentation having been exchanged and depositions scheduled to continue into February.
Radisys shares fell sharply Friday after it told analysts the SEC had requested documents related to the company's inventory accounting.

In July 1996, Bruce Taylor, a former vice president of operations, sued RadiSys, alleging he uncovered "a significant discrepency in the financial records of RadiSys" related to the reporting of the company's inventory.

RadiSys said in November 1996 it received inquiries on the lawsuit and on whether it had been contacted by the SEC. It had not been contacted by the SEC at that time, but said it subsequently contacted the SEC to volunteer full cooperation.
RadiSys said the SEC later asked it to provide it with supporting documentation for its financial statements and certain additional data related to the allegations.

RadiSys said it promptly provided the SEC with all of the requested documents and has not been contacted by the SEC since complying with its request. It said intends to cooperate fully with any inquiry from the SEC in the future.
The company said the SEC's letter stated that the request "should not be construed as an adverse reflection on any person, security, issuer, or transaction."
RadiSys shares fell 10 to 47-1/2 in late afternoon trading Friday.
